title: Primary-process emotion survives removal of the neocortex

statements.text: All primary-process emotional urges, even ones as complex as social PLAY, remain intact after radical removal of the neocortex early in life, so the neocortex is not needed to generate primary-process emotion. Decorticated animals are, if anything, more emotional than normal.

sources.quote: the neocortex is not essential for the generation of primary-process emotionality
these animals are actually more emotional than normal
